entries.title: Single Beam Splitting for enhanced Denisyuk reflections
entries.excerpt: Beam splitting and “single beam” holography “Single beam” holography commonly known as Denisyuk or reflection holography is really a misnomer because of course all holography involves the interaction of never less than 2 beams from a single source. entries.title: Holography is not lensless photography.
entries.excerpt: Some sources allege holography as being a "lensless photography." I disagree, for the following reason. entries.title: Measuring hardness of gelatin.

entries.title: Helping your working developer last longer
entries.excerpt: Similar to Tom over here, I've been using tupperware and locking containers for a while and just started using a combination of that and Wine Savers to make my working developer last longer. In a nutshell, cut a hole in the top of your container and glue a wine saver stopper into the hole. Now you can use the pump to remove a lot of the air inside the container and your working developer will last longer before you have to throw it out. entries.title: Food for thought - Color Holography

entries.title: Disposal of old dichromate baths
entries.excerpt: It is not permitted to pour dichromate down the sink, it is really a quite toxic material as it is a real flora and fauna killer. But you can kill it's toxicity by chucking it into a container with your old developer solutions. That instantly converts it to an insoluble sludge of basic CrIII compounds. Don't put a lid back on the container tightly though as CO2 gas needs to come off from your carbonate and acid reaction. [/b]

entries.title: Brewsters Angle

They mention it is about 56 degrees but not where the 56 degrees is measureed from. Intuitively one thinks of normal being 90 degrees so 56 degrees is 34 degrees off normal and this is INCORRECT! To arrive at Brewsters angle for glass in holography, measure 56 degrees off the nomal.

entries.title: Incident Angle Measuring Device
entries.excerpt: A nail stuck at right angles in a piece of cardboard or plexiglass makes a great angle measuring device for spread beams. This fleshed-out normal (or gnomon, in sundial terms, notice the root word) casts a shadow on the substrate. When the shadow is the same size as the nail, the angle of incidence is 45 degrees. Drawing concentric circles whose radii are the tangent of the angle times the height of the nail gives you other angles of incidence. For instance, the shadow cast by a 25 mm nail with…

entries.title: Simple Metering
entries.excerpt: For a fairly cheap and very simple Hene light meter, use the Radio Shack Solar Cell, 276-124, and a DVM. Total area of this cell is 8 cm2. For low light levels, place a 215 ohm resistor in parallel with the solar cell and measure the voltage. At low levels (below 100mV), the response of this is .5mV/uW/cm2. For undiverged Hene beams, just measure current output directly. The conversion is .47 ma/mW. The above quoted numbers are compared to an OPT101P. Sensitivity at wavelengths other than 633nm…

entries.title: Photographing a Hologram

entries.title: Painting Plates
entries.excerpt: Here's my technique for painting the emulsion side of H2 reflection copies: I tape the plate emulsion side up to a piece of white typing paper. The goal is to mask the plate so no overspray gets on the front side. I run a piece of masking tape along each edge, with 1/32" overlap. Then I run my fingernail along the edge of the plate, forcing the masking tape to pull back from the plate but adhere to the edge of the glass. This way I can get total coverage of the emulsion side. entries.title: Effects of a spatial filter

However, I extended that to understand that the resulting hologram would be therefore freer of distortions like random rings and artifacts. Recent discussion has led me to believe that a spatial filter increases the smoothness of textures, the ability to resolve detail, and the overall clarity of the hologram. entries.title: Time Smear
entries.excerpt: I am looking for a theoretical understanding for the effect of time smear in a multiplex hologram. Can anyone explain it to me or provide me with a reference? For those who do not know, time smear is where the motion (in a hologram that is best described by the terms "multiplexed holographically encoded stereogram") blurs because the motion is faster than can be portrayed by the medium. Classic examples are Liti's work as well as Loyd Cross' work.

entries.title: beam ratio for Denisyuks
entries.excerpt: To determine the beam ratio for a single beam Denisyuk. Make a small ish hole a white card.. Place the card in the plateholder and hit it with the reference beam. The central area of the beam goes through the hole ands scatters off the object onto the back of the card. By visually examining the front and back of the card, you can determine how much the object beam is and where it's going.

entries.title: determining the best density for your plate
entries.excerpt: Make a series of strips in your graphics program (eg photoshop ) with each one a fixed amount darker than the previous using greyscale mode. Tape these to the wall of your processing area. As you process, compare the film darkness against these strips. When you find a darkness that works well, not the strip number and always develop to the darkness of that strip.

entries.title: Holography and Solar Cells
entries.excerpt: A while ago I was doing some research on Solar Cells for another project I was doing and found some interesting data on solar cells. Most solar cells are wavelength selective, as in the Amorphous Solar Cells, and their spectral response reaches maximum at the wavelengths of blue light. Longer wavelengths only heat the cell causing faster degradation. So why not cover with a narrow band blue wavelength transmission HOE?

entries.title: Rainbow masters
entries.excerpt: It's usually standard practice to have an H1 for rainbows as long and narrow. You could have a 7 x 2.5 for the H1 and a slit width of less than 2.5 in. along the '7' side, ie a slit 7 in long and about 1/2 in wide. The problem is that once you've made an H1 with these dimensions, you can't ever use it for anything else but rainbows. If you want the flexibility of using the H1 for anything at all, use the full 5x7. If you know that the H1 is only going to be used for rainbows, use te 7 x 2.5.

entries.title: Ion Laser Question
entries.excerpt: This is really strange. Last week I was using my 514 line. I tuned it for max power (mirrors) and did not touct the already tuned etalon for 488. Interferometer was great. Then a couple of days ago I decided to go back to 488. I left the etalon alone and peaked for 488 and I got a non Tem00 mode at peak power (thumbscrew tuning not power dial on power supply). The beam had a black spot in the center of it. When I detuned on of the mirrors slightly the black spot went away. Fringes were great…
